summary: This Old House guides a homeowner through diagnosing and fixing a noisy hydronic baseboard heating system. The host explains how a closed-loop boiler system circulates 180°F water through copper baseboard fins, with a return line circulating back to the boiler. The team identifies that the noise stems from copper pipe expansion pushing a long return line against an exterior wall and deforming drywall. They isolate a single zone, drain the top-floor baseboard, and shorten the return pipe to allow room for expansion. Using an emery cloth to clean the pipe, a tight-spaces tubing cutter (Imp), flux, and careful reassembly, they realign the return with the supply line, refill the system, and verify that the baseboards operate quietly with no audible noise.
